FACT_ID: sec06-R01 | anchor: A03
A U.S. route shield displaying 22 identifies U.S. Traffic Route 22. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R02 | anchor: A03
A keystone route marker displaying 39 identifies Pennsylvania Traffic Route 39. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R03 | anchor: A03
A JCT plate above a route marker announces an approaching intersection with that route. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R04 | anchor: A03
A WEST plate above a U.S. Route 22 marker indicates westbound travel on that route. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R05 | anchor: A03
A right-turn arrow below a WEST U.S. Route 22 assembly warns that continuing on that route requires the upcoming right turn. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R06 | anchor: A03
A TO plate with a U.S. Route 22 marker and an upward arrow directs continued straight travel to reach that route. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R07 | anchor: A03
Service signs use blue backgrounds with white letters or symbols, have square or rectangular shapes, and identify services at the next exit. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R08 | anchor: A03
Service symbols can identify a hospital, telephone, food, gasoline, diesel or lodging. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R09 | anchor: A03
Tourist directional signs are squares or rectangles with white lettering on blue or brown. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R10 | anchor: A03
Tourist directional signs guide traffic to attractions such as museums, historic landmarks and state or national parks. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R11 | anchor: A04
Permanent pavement markings identify road centers, lanes, edges and special lane uses. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-R12 | anchor: A04
Yellow pavement lines separate opposing directions of traffic. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-R13 | anchor: A04
Yellow lines mark the center of two-lane roads and the left edge of divided highways, one-way streets and ramps. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-R14 | anchor: A04
Solid white pavement lines separate same-direction lanes and also mark a roadway's right edge. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-R15 | anchor: A04
As a general rule, broken traffic lines may be crossed and solid lines may not, except when making a turn. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-R16 | anchor: A04
A single broken yellow centerline on a two-way, two-lane road permits passing from either side only when conditions are safe. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-R17 | anchor: A04
Passing across a broken yellow centerline uses the lane for oncoming traffic. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-R18 | anchor: A04
A double solid yellow centerline prohibits passing in either direction even without a NO PASSING sign. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-R19 | anchor: A04
With one solid and one broken yellow centerline, passing is allowed from the broken-line side only when conditions are safe. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-R20 | anchor: A04
With one solid and one broken yellow centerline, the driver on the solid-line side may not pass. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-R21 | anchor: A04
A shared center turn lane bordered by solid outer and broken inner yellow lines is reserved for left turns from either direction and cannot be used for passing. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-R22 | anchor: A04
On an undivided multilane road, broken white lane lines may be crossed to pass when the passing lane is clear. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-R23 | anchor: A04
On an undivided multilane road, a double yellow centerline cannot be crossed for passing and opposing traffic lies beyond it. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-R24 | anchor: A04
On the usual divided limited-access highway pattern, solid white marks the right edge and solid yellow marks the left edge of each roadway. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-R25 | anchor: A04
Broken white lines between same-direction lanes on a divided limited-access highway may be crossed. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-R26 | anchor: A04
Pavement words and arrows supplement regulatory and warning signs. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-R27 | anchor: A04
STOP AHEAD pavement wording announces a stop-sign intersection ahead. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-R28 | anchor: A04
YIELD wording or white triangles across a lane indicate that the driver must yield to approaching traffic. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-R29 | anchor: A04
SCHOOL pavement wording warns of a school zone ahead. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-R30 | anchor: A04
R X R pavement lettering marks an approaching railroad crossing. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-R31 | anchor: A04
BIKE LANE pavement wording identifies a lane reserved for bicyclists. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-R32 | anchor: A04
ONLY combined with a left or right pavement arrow reserves the lane for that turn. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-R33 | anchor: A04
Large white pavement arrows indicate travel direction on one-way roads and highway exit ramps. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0026]
